name: Voltage measuring transducer
summary: Transducer that converts a VT secondary or direct voltage into an isolated analogue signal for remote measurement.
description: A voltage measuring transducer converts a voltage into a standard analogue signal such as 4-20 mA, with galvanic isolation between input and output. It is fed from a VT secondary or, at low voltage, directly from the busbar through fuses, and it supplies a PLC, SCADA or regulator input.

The symbol does not show whether the output follows RMS or average value, or the live zero of the output range. If the transducer is self-powered from the measured voltage, its output fails when the voltage collapses, which matters when it is used to detect loss of supply.
readingNotes: Check whether the transducer has a separate auxiliary supply.
Confirm the output range and live zero.
distinction: A voltage transducer provides a signal to other equipment; a voltmeter displays the reading locally.
